div.l: Who so ys Rebell / to my Iugement prologꝰus
Shal paye for al / that bi the wey is spent
Now draweth cut / er we ferther twynne
He that hath the shortest / shall begynne
Sere knyht ꝙquod he / my maist̉er and my lorde
Now draweth cut / for this is myn accorde
Cometh neer ꝙquod he / my lady prioresse
And ye sir clerk / and let be you shamfastnesse
Ne studyeth nat / leyth / hond to / everyman
A noon to drawe / every whiht be gan
And shortly for to tellen / as it was
Wer it bi aventure / or sort or caas
The soth is this / the cut fel to the knyht
Of whiche wel blyyth / and glad was eủery wyht
And telle he must his tale / bi reson
By forward / and bi composicion
As ye han hard / what nedyth wordys moo
And whanne this good man / saw that it was so
As he that wys was / and obedient
To kepe his forward / bi his free assent
He seid syn / I shall begynne this game
What wolcom be the cut / a godys name
Nowe lat vs ryde / and harkeneth what I say
And wᵗith. that word / we redyn forth our way
And hehe bigan / wᵗith ryht a mery chere
His tale a noon / and seyd as ye may here .
Here begennyth the knyhtys tale.
Som tyme / as olde Storyes tellyn vs
Ther was a duk / that hyht Theseus knyght
Of Athenes / he was lord and gouernour
And in his tyme / suche a conquerour
That grettere was ther noon vnder the sonne
